incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: France – Code de commerce (Commercial Code), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company formation); Articles L.225-113 to L.225-135 mutatis mutandis on subscription and payment of share capital; Décret n°2021-1621 and implementing texts on the single digital window (Guichet unique); Article R.123-31 on the contents of the incorporation filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Paris: Tribunal de Commerce de Paris); filings are received through the national single window (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the INPI. The certified identity extract issued is the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (electronic single incorporation declaration) submitted on the Guichet unique, accompanied by the executed Statuts (Articles of Association), the bank attestation of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds), the certificate of publication of the legal formation notice, and the President's declaration of no criminal conviction.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A French SAS has no statutory minimum capital. The present entity is formed with EUR 10,000 share capital; every cash subscriber must pay at least 50% of the subscribed value at incorporation. The funds must be deposited into a temporarily blocked escrow account held with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and are released only after registration (obtention of the Kbis). Contributions in kind must be fully delivered at incorporation; the unpaid balance may be called within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY], A SOCIÉTÉ PAR ACTIONS SIMPLIFIÉE. Pursuant to Articles L.227-1 and L.227-9 of the French Commercial Code, the undersigned founding shareholders unanimously resolve as follows: (1) The initial share capital of EUR 10,000, comprising 10,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each, is fully subscribed and paid in cash. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Paris, France. (3) [Name] is appointed President for an indefinite term with the full powers of Article L.227-6. (4) The President is authorized to deposit funds with a bank, order the legal announcement, file the incorporation dossier at the Guichet unique, and resolve registry queries. This resolution shall be recorded in the minutes register and is effective immediately. Paris, [date].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique (France); official portal: impots.gouv.fr; company law and statutory filings via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and the RCS (Infogreffe).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) French SAS: incorporate through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises; the RCS Greffe assigns SIREN/SIRET, INSEE updates the national register, and DGFiP automatically issues the French tax identification number and intra-Community VAT number (FR + key + SIREN). (2) Foreign non-established entity with French VAT obligations: file the DGFiP non-resident VAT/TIN registration (commonly Form 1554-SD) with the territorial Service des Impôts des Entreprises, attaching certificate of incorporation, apostilled/legalized status evidence, foreign tax number, constitutional documents, and description of French taxable activities; DGFiP issues the French TIN/VAT identification number. (3) A non-EU or EU supplier of B2C electronic services may instead use the OSS/IOSS and must obtain an OSS registration number in an EU member state; full French VAT registration is required if the OSS cannot be used or the supply is outside OSS scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for an SAS. An SAS is statutorily subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés), with a territoriality rule exempting profits attributable to foreign permanent establishments. Optional elections include: (i) French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale, CGI Art. 223 A) for a 95%+ French subgroup; (ii) VAT grouping (assujetti unique, CGI Art. 256 C III) for qualifying closely-linked French taxable persons; (iii) election to apply or not apply the parent-subsidiary dividend exemption; and (iv) in cross-border structures, procedural options to elect transparent treatment of a foreign entity are generally denied; hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and cannot be elected around.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA) under the EU VAT Directive, implemented by Code général des impôts, Articles 256 to 260 quinquies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established small businesses, annual taxable turnover of EUR 85,000 (goods) or EUR 37,500 (services) for the franchise en base de TVA exemption; above those thresholds, subject to tolerance bands, French VAT registration is mandatory. For non-established suppliers there is no turnover threshold; any taxable supply of digital services to French consumers triggers French VAT via OSS/IOSS or direct registration. The EU-wide distance-sale/e-service threshold of EUR 10,000 applies to EU-established suppliers using the Union OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured e-invoicing for domestic B2B transactions through certified Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDPs) linked to DGFiP's Public Portal (PPF). From 1 September 2026, large and medium issuers must issue e-invoices and all taxpayers must receive them; small issuers are required from 1 September 2027. The system uses API e-reporting and central collection, not real-time tax-authority clearance or digital stamping/QR-code validation; B2C transaction data is reported electronically to DGFiP.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Tangible goods physically exported from France to a destination outside the European Union are eligible for 0% French VAT under CGI Art. 262 I 1° and EU VAT Directive Art. 146 where the seller demonstrates dispatch and the goods leave the EU under a valid customs export declaration. Supporting documentation must evidence the commercial transaction, export of the goods, and the physical exit from EU territory. Electronic/EdTech services are not 'goods exports': cross-border B2B services are generally taxable at the customer's place of establishment and B2C e-services to French consumers are taxed in France via OSS, not zero-rated; where the place of supply is outside France, the supply is merely outside the scope of French VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation / EXS) accepted by French Customs, including the MRN
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (Air Waybill/CMR) proving physical removal from France/EU
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank/FX records matching the export invoice, payment and MRN
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French Customs may audit export zero-rating retrospectively within the statutory limitation period. If the export file lacks mandatory documentation or is fraudulent, the administration recharacterizes the supply as French taxable and assesses 20% VAT on the invoice value, adds late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, and applies penalties of 40% for bad faith or 80% for fraud or tax maneuvers. False customs declarations may incur customs penalties, confiscation and criminal exposure; refunded VAT can be clawed back with interest, and the reassessment period is extended in cases of fraud or undisclosed activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision; exchange control policy is administered by the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the Eurozone; the Euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange control restrictions apply to non-resident investors or to the repatriation of profits, dividends, or capital. Profit remittance is subject to standard corporate income tax (25% standard rate) and, where applicable, withholding tax on dividends (25% under domestic law, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parent companies). No prior administrative authorization is required for capital movements, except for certain transactions involving non-EU countries that may require statistical reporting to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency in designated accounts (comptes en devises) or convert to EUR at their discretion. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts, nor any mandatory conversion ratio. However, all cross-border transactions exceeding €50,000 must be reported to the Banque de France for statistical balance-of-payments purposes, typically via the intermediary bank. For EdTech subscription revenues (digital services), the applicable VAT rules (reverse charge for B2B, place of supply rules for B2C) are separate from FX controls.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR) and Capital Escrow Account (if required for investor funds)
Operational Account (EUR) and Treasury Management Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) under the ACPR licensing regime (transposing the EU PSD2 and EMD2 directives). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK-based or non-EU) may operate in France only under a passporting regime (for EU/EEA entities) or via a French branch/agent. For a French SAS, using a fully licensed French EMI (e.g., Qonto, Shine, or Treezor) is viable for day-to-day treasury operations, but for large cross-border capital injections and trade settlements, a tier-1 commercial bank is recommended due to higher counterparty limits and SWIFT capabilities. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide credit or hold client funds beyond the e-money float; they are not suitable for escrow or complex FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for SAS directors, but most tier-1 French banks require at least one physical meeting (or a notarized identity verification) for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and signatories. Remote onboarding is possible via video identification (e.g., via ACPR-approved e-IDV providers) for certain banks, but the final compliance sign-off often requires a physical visit to a branch or a bank representative. For non-resident directors, banks may require a local agent or a French registered office address. The KYC interview (in person or via secure video) is mandatory for all UBOs holding >25% of shares or control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction for UBOs or counterparties (e.g., non-OECD countries, tax havens)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) UBO declaration form (Formulaire UBO) filed with the French Trade Registry (RCS); (2) Certified copies of passports and proof of address; (3) Source of wealth documentation (bank statements, tax returns, audited financials); (4) Business plan and commercial contracts demonstrating legitimate EdTech operations; (5) Negative media screening report from a reputable provider (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., high-volume subscription receipts from multiple jurisdictions, rapid in/out flows)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Detailed business model explanation with revenue flow diagrams; (2) Subscription agreements and terms of service; (3) Payment processor statements (Apple IAP, Google Play) showing merchant ID and settlement reports; (4) Tax registration certificates (VAT, corporate tax) and proof of filing; (5) A formal AML/CFT risk assessment and internal controls policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient corporate substance (e.g., no physical office, no employees in France)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Lease agreement or virtual office contract with a French address; (2) Employment contracts or payroll records for at least one local director or employee; (3) Board resolutions authorizing the bank account and treasury operations; (4) Business plan demonstrating local market presence; (5) Evidence of French VAT registration and compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or high-risk payment processor involvement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Written confirmation that the company does not accept crypto assets; (2) Contracts with regulated payment processors (Apple, Google) and their compliance certifications; (3) Transaction monitoring reports; (4) Legal opinion from a French counsel on the business model's compliance with the French Monetary and Financial Code.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Inbound capital injections (shareholder loans or equity contributions) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with a clear purpose code. For France, the Banque de France requires a 'Motif de l'opération' (purpose code) for balance-of-payments reporting. Standard codes: 'S010' for equity capital contributions, 'S020' for shareholder loans (if >€50,000). The remitter must include the company's SIREN number and the nature of the transaction. Verification: The receiving bank will request a copy of the share subscription agreement, board resolution, and proof of identity of the investor. For non-EU investors, a French bank may require a 'Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds' (DTF) form to be filed with the Banque de France within 20 days of the transaction. The funds must be credited to a designated EUR account; no prior FX approval is needed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For EdTech subscription payments to foreign content providers, software licensors, or marketing agencies, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for direct payments. For recurring high-volume disbursements, a SEPA Direct Debit (SDD) or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is used for EU counterparties. For non-EU trade settlements, commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are rarely used for service-based EdTech; instead, open account with SWIFT MT103 is standard. For larger contracts, a standby LC (SBLC) may be issued by the French bank to guarantee payment. All outbound transfers must include a purpose code (e.g., 'S030' for service payments, 'S040' for royalties). The bank will verify the underlying contract and may require a proforma invoice. For payments to sanctioned jurisdictions, the bank will block the transaction; a compliance review is mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain vanilla) with a maturity up to 12 months, available from tier-1 banks for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY, and other major pairs. No underlying trade documentation required for amounts below €1 million; above that, a commercial contract is needed.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are permissible for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., INR, KRW, TWD) but are rarely used for EUR-based EdTech companies; they are available via major banks with a special approval from the French Treasury for hedging purposes only.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) are permissible for long-term hedging (over 1 year) of foreign currency debt or investment flows. Requires a detailed risk management policy and board approval. The bank will require an ISDA Master Agreement and a Credit Support Annex (CSA).
FX Options (plain vanilla calls/puts) are permissible for hedging subscription revenue volatility, but are subject to the bank's internal risk appetite and may require a premium payment upfront.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profits or losses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder; no routine filing with an authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a permitted extension is obtained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the company and its legal representative to complete approval; the legal representative may incur civil or, in specified cases, criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing, including the management report where filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial and Companies Register through the competent commercial court registry (greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president of the commercial court may issue an injunction, including a penalty payment; the company may also be fined up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat offenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and required schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally by the second working day after 1 May, subject to the applicable filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after a formal notice is not remedied within 30 days, plus late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate real-estate tax (CFE) declaration and annual payment, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally payable by 15 December; an installment is generally due by 15 June if the prior-year assessment exceeded EUR 3,000. An initial declaration is generally due by 31 December of the year of establishment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally incurs a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest. Amounts depend on the local assessment and applicable exemptions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update, if reportable particulars change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial and Companies Register through the competent commercial court registry (greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the company becomes aware of a change requiring an update; no routine annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership information may result in criminal fines and other statutory penalties for the company and responsible individuals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of these three thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 employees. Separate rules may require an auditor for specified group relationships or other statutory circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the French General Chart of Accounts (Plan comptable général); IFRS is generally not required for an unlisted SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France has no routine annual beneficial ownership confirmation. The SAS must file an update within 30 days after a reportable change. Share transfers must be recorded in the applicable securities movement records and reflected in the share register; annual accounts approval does not replace these duties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholders and share movement records
Minute book recording shareholder and corporate decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 220–870 annually for basic commercial domiciliation; fees vary by location and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,300–11,000 annually for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; complexity and group reporting can increase fees.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax. A reduced 15% rate may apply to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small companies, generally subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% individual ownership or qualifying equivalent ownership.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small companies may obtain the 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit. Research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure incurred in France and certain EU states up to EUR 100 million of annual eligible expenditure, subject to statutory conditions. The innovation tax credit may apply to qualifying SME innovation expenditure. Tax holidays or investment incentives depend on location, activity, employee status, and approval conditions. France also permits tax consolidation for qualifying groups and provides participation exemption treatment for qualifying dividends, generally with a 5% add-back of expenses and charges.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. Use of carried-forward tax losses is generally capped annually at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. A tax loss carryback election is generally limited to the immediately preceding fiscal year and capped at the lower of that year's profit or EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and annexes for corporate income tax, filed electronically through the French Tax Administration professional portal or by EDI-TDFC through an authorized partner. The annual tax package generally includes Forms 2058-A, 2058-B, 2058-C, 2058-F, 2059-A to 2059-G, and applicable sector or group schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four corporate income tax instalments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May, subject to the applicable electronic-filing extension. For other year-ends, the return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, fiscal year dates, tax office, tax regime, and filing capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS legal and tax identification details. A foreign shareholder is not itself entered as the taxpayer unless it operates a taxable French permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability, turnover, accounting period, tax regime, and applicable reduced-rate or group-tax information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French company's worldwide taxable results under French rules. A nonresident parent must not include its foreign profits in the SAS return absent a French taxable presence attributable to those profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or tax loss, including permanent and temporary adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses attributable to the SAS and supported by French accounting records, contracts, invoices, and business purpose. Adjust non-deductible expenses, withholding taxes, penalties, provisions, and transfer-pricing corrections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses used, remaining losses, and any carryback election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the annual EUR 1 million plus 50% limitation. Maintain separate support for pre-acquisition losses, changes in activity, and losses potentially lost following a material change of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits where applicable, and amounts carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally available to the French SAS. Foreign tax credits generally require treaty or statutory authority and documentary proof of foreign tax paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain transactions with related entities, including capital relationships and material financial or commercial links.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify relevant foreign parent, subsidiaries, sister companies, financing entities, licensors, and service providers, consistently with transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholdings, qualifying participation interests, and relevant disposal information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material French and foreign participations held by the SAS and apply participation-exemption rules only where statutory conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain extraordinary, non-deductible, or non-routine expenses, including specified management and luxury expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include payments to foreign affiliates or executives where required, particularly expenses lacking commercial justification or falling within restricted deductibility categories.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of transfer-pricing policy, controlled transactions, methods, amounts, and documentation status where the filing obligation applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all reported amounts to the general ledger, intercompany agreements, invoices, and Local File. Disclose material cross-border controlled transactions even where the counterparty is in a treaty jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and payment of each corporate income tax instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS tax reference and payment account. An overseas shareholder has no payment obligation unless separately liable for French tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax balance after crediting instalments and eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065 and the annual tax package. Pay any residual amount by the statutory deadline; do not offset unrelated foreign taxes without legal authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning distributions, withholding obligations, and certain payments to nonresidents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French domestic withholding unless a treaty or EU exemption is properly supported. Retain residence certificates, beneficial-ownership evidence, forms, and payment records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment generally triggers a 10% surcharge. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month or fraction of a month, subject to statutory rules. Deliberate failure may trigger a 40% penalty; fraudulent maneuver or abuse of rights may trigger an 80% penalty. Inaccurate returns may attract penalties based on the taxpayer's intent and the tax administration's assessment. Criminal tax-fraud exposure may arise in aggravated cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD annual corporate income tax return and electronic tax package through the professional tax portal or EDI-TDFC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due under the applicable fiscal-year deadline, generally the second business day following 1 May for a 31 December year-end or within three months after other year-ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, legal form, registered office, fiscal year, and tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS is the filing entity. Enter the foreign parent only in related-party, shareholder, or distribution disclosures where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss after French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include revenue from subscriptions, application stores, licensing, tutoring software, advertising, and ancillary services earned by the SAS, subject to applicable revenue-recognition and permanent-establishment analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable bases, applicable rates, gross tax, tax credits, instalments, and balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% rate unless a documented statutory reduced rate or credit applies. Do not treat foreign-parent tax as a French corporate income tax credit without legal support.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: The general 10% late-filing surcharge and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest may apply. Additional penalties may apply for omissions, materially incorrect information, abusive arrangements, or obstruction of a tax audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD corporate income tax instalment statement and payment through the French professional tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The first year may have no instalment or a reduced obligation depending on the company's incorporation date and expected liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year corporate income tax or current-year estimate, as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SAS's French corporate income tax liability. Foreign shareholder profitability does not enter the instalment calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, prior instalments, amount due, and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all credits are legally transferable or claimable by the SAS and reconcile payment references with the French tax account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally triggers 10% surcharge and 0.20% monthly interest. Underpayment caused by an inaccurate estimate may result in a balance due and audit exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD corporate income tax balance statement and payment through the French professional tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax, instalments, credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile to the filed 2065 package and retain payment confirmations, tax-credit substantiation, and board approval of the accounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally results in a 10% surcharge and 0.20% monthly interest. Additional penalties may apply if the balance is understated through negligence or deliberate conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a nonresident. Exemption or reduction may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, subject generally to a qualifying holding of at least 10%, minimum holding-period and anti-abuse conditions, or under an applicable tax treaty. The domestic rate for certain French-resident individual recipients is different and does not determine the nonresident corporate rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, legal form, holding percentage, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose restrictions, and anti-conduit requirements. Use the applicable French administrative form or treaty procedure for reduced or zero withholding, retain supporting documents, and report and remit withholding through the French withholding return. If relief cannot be secured before payment, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund claim with the French tax administration where treaty conditions are satisfied. Treaty relief does not apply merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to nonresidents may generally be subject to French withholding at 25% under domestic rules, subject to treaty allocation, EU interest-and-royalty relief where applicable, and anti-abuse conditions. Interest paid by a French company to a nonresident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding under domestic law, but special rules may apply to payments to non-cooperative states or territories, certain hybrid or anti-abuse arrangements, and specific regulated instruments. Treaty rates vary, commonly providing reduced rates or exclusive residence-state taxation. Arm's-length pricing, beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, and deductibility must be separately established.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million. Comprehensive Local File and Master File obligations generally apply where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, where it owns or is owned directly or indirectly by an entity meeting that threshold, or where statutory related-party conditions otherwise apply. Entities below the threshold may still be required to provide simplified transfer-pricing documentation and evidence of arm's-length pricing upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate general economic-substance regulation regime equivalent to a standalone ESR statute. Substance is assessed through transfer-pricing rules, the French general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, principal-purpose testing under treaties, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, anti-hybrid provisions, permanent-establishment principles, and EU anti-abuse law. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or functional infrastructure, commercial risk control, accounting records, and demonstrable functions consistent with its EdTech activities. A conduit entity with no meaningful functions, risks, or control may suffer denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization, withholding, transfer-pricing adjustments, penalties, and joint or secondary liability.
sector_specific_transfer_pricing_control: Benchmark subscription, software-development, cloud, customer-support, marketing, licensing, and management-service transactions separately where functions and risks differ.
Document ownership and development of algorithms, software, trademarks, teaching content, customer data, and other intangibles under a DEMPE analysis.
Reconcile Apple App Store and Google Play settlement statements, commissions, refunds, chargebacks, indirect taxes, and intercompany revenue allocations to the statutory accounts.
Use a consistent policy for foreign-parent services, platform royalties, software licenses, financing, and cost recharges; unsupported management fees are high-risk deductions.
Maintain contemporaneous intercompany agreements, invoices, timesheets, technical evidence, allocation keys, market comparables, and payment trails.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false corporate income tax filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing subscription revenue, omitting application-store income, fabricating expenses, falsely claiming tax credits, or deliberately understating taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 10% to 80% tax penalties depending on conduct, 0.20% monthly late-payment interest, and possible criminal tax-fraud prosecution. Aggravated tax fraud may lead to imprisonment of up to seven years and substantial criminal fines, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur criminal liability for personal participation, civil liability for intentional misconduct or mismanagement, tax liability as a de facto manager in appropriate proceedings, and potential disqualification from management. A travel ban or imprisonment is possible only under applicable criminal or judicial measures and is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting French profit to a low-tax affiliate through excessive royalties, management fees, financing charges, underpriced IP transfers, or non-arm's-length platform arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reintegration of understated French profits, withholding-tax assessment, interest, penalties, documentation penalties, and possible denial of treaty benefits or tax-credit claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for deliberate mismanagement or participation in fraudulent arrangements. Criminal exposure requires proof of an underlying offense such as tax fraud, forgery, corruption, or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a foreign conduit lacking personnel, functions, risk control, beneficial ownership, or commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU exemption, withholding at domestic rates, abuse-of-law adjustment, interest, and penalties up to the statutory maximum for abusive conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for knowing participation in abusive or fraudulent conduct. Courts may impose management bans or criminal measures where separate criminal offenses are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other reportable cross-border amounts without withholding, without collecting residence documentation, or without filing the required withholding return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding from the French payer, late-payment interest, applicable penalties, and possible liability for incorrect or omitted withholding declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed in cases of fraudulent concealment, gross misconduct, or criminal participation; ordinary company-level withholding errors do not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete French accounting records, unsupported journal entries, missing invoices, unreliable intercompany ledgers, or inability to reconcile payment-processor data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax-base estimation, rejection of deductions, penalties, audit extension, accounting sanctions, and possible criminal liability for falsified accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors have statutory duties regarding proper accounts and may face civil claims, management liability, or criminal prosecution for intentional falsification or obstruction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to distinguish B2B and B2C digital services, misidentifying customer location, incorrectly treating Apple or Google as the principal supplier, or omitting EU One Stop Shop obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, interest, penalties, denied deductions, joint-and-several collection in specified cases, and possible registration or reporting sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for deliberate fraud, organized concealment, or serious management misconduct, but ordinary VAT errors remain primarily corporate liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained funds, using nominee shareholders, making undisclosed related-party payments, disguising kickbacks as consulting fees, or failing to identify beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting, account restrictions, confiscation, AML fines, tax reassessment, and criminal money-laundering penalties. Money laundering may carry imprisonment and substantial fines depending on the offense and aggravating factors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face criminal prosecution, asset confiscation, management bans, travel restrictions, and imprisonment where personal knowledge or participation is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering or accepting improper advantages through agents, distributors, education partners, public institutions, or technology procurement channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, debarment, damages, and corporate compliance obligations under French anti-corruption law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may face criminal imprisonment, fines, professional disqualification, travel restrictions, and civil restitution. The company may incur separate criminal fines and compliance-monitoring measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of corporate assets and unlawful distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using SAS funds for personal expenses, paying dividends without distributable profits, concealing losses, or transferring assets to shareholders or affiliates without consideration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment, cancellation of unlawful distributions, civil damages, shareholder claims, insolvency consequences, and criminal sanctions for abuse of corporate assets where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for restitution and damages and may face imprisonment, fines, and management bans under the applicable French corporate and criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to incur debts while insolvent, preferring related parties, disposing of assets below value, failing to file for insolvency when required, or withholding books and records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Clawback of transactions, insolvency proceedings, director contribution to insufficient assets, bankruptcy-related penalties, and possible criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute personally to the company's shortfall, prohibited from managing companies, and imprisoned or fined for specified bankruptcy offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Obstruction of tax audit or destruction of evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Refusing access to books, deleting emails or accounting data, backdating intercompany agreements, concealing servers, or providing knowingly false information to the tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Separate procedural penalties, estimated assessment, increased tax penalties, evidentiary presumptions, and possible criminal prosecution for obstruction, forgery, or tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct or authorize obstruction may face personal fines, criminal prosecution, management bans, travel restrictions, and imprisonment where legally established.
